input:
You are queen_d1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 20. the team planned Qc5 (queen_d1), but queen_d1 (amnesia) sent Qd3 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 7. the team planned bxa5 (pawn_b2), but pawn_b2 (amnesia) sent b5 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 10. the team planned e4 (pawn_e2), but pawn_e2 (amnesia) sent e3 instead, and that move was played, costing 28 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending any move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send a move only if your piece is the one named and the move matches the plan exactly; if your piece is not the planned mover, stay silent even when threatened or a capture is available, unless the chat explicitly calls for it.
- Before sending your move, copy the planned move from chat and compare it character by character with the move you are about to send (piece and destination square), and send only if they match exactly; if they differ, stop and do not send.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending, the planned mover must write the exact planned move (piece and destination square) back into chat and then send exactly that move and nothing else, and every other agent must stay silent and not send any move unless the chat explicitly names their piece, even if their piece is threatened or can capture.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
